messages:
Ana: FYI: Pelican-13B int4 onboard smoke done. Cost looks great but seeing upstream coherence drops on our multi-turn convo evals.
Rohit: how large are the dropoffs?
Ana: on convo-coherence suite: ~6% hit in turn-to-turn consistency (mostly 4th+ turns). Single-turn QA fine.
Sam: int4 quant sometimes loses KV fidelity for long contexts — are we prefetching full past context into KV?
Ana: we enable aggressive prefetch to keep latency low, prefetch_limit=2048 tokens, kv.keep_recent=8192. Logs show lots of small alloc/free.
Hannah: can you paste a snippet of the allocation trace?
Ana: pasted: 
```
[2024-09-10T11:02:12Z] gen:start model=pelican-13b-int4 req_id=abc123 ctx_len=4096 gen=512
[2024-09-10T11:02:12Z] prefetch: queued 20 chunks (avg 48KB)
[2024-09-10T11:02:12Z] alloc: requested 850MB, free_contig=600MB
[2024-09-10T11:02:12Z] alloc: split_alloc small_chunk=32KB
[2024-09-10T11:02:12Z] OOM: allocation failed after splits, aborting
```
Rohit: small_chunk churn -> fragmentation. Possible mitigations: reduce prefetch_limit, enable per-session kv.trim_threshold, and use compaction.
Sam: also try lowering max_new_tokens for long-context endpoints — when generation is long + large ctx, int4's per-token working set is higher due to dequant/scale buffers.
Ana: suggested quick experiments:
- prefetch_limit -> 1024
- kv.trim_threshold -> 0.7
- compactor.enable=true, compactor.rate=0.2
- default max_new_tokens for convo endpoints -> 256
Rohit: add targeted evals: convo-coherence-long (ctx 4k+) and latency/p95. Keep unit-cost baseline.
Ana: running rbench now:
```
rbench --model pelican-13b-int4 --suite convo-coherence-long --concurrency 12 --batch-cap 6 --max_new_tokens 256 --prefetch_limit 1024
```
Ops-bot: perf job queued -> https://ci.internal/runs/8192 (artifacts + token breakdown)
Ana: first 5k requests no OOMs; coherence drop reduced to ~1.5% (was 6%). p95 latency slightly up (~6%); cost/token still ~2.8x lower vs fp16.
Sam: 6% -> 1.5% is good. Can we try hybrid quant profile for convo endpoints (keep attention/kv in int8 or fp16 while weights int4)? That often restores coherence.
Rohit: agree. We can try "mixed-dequant": attention-kv-precision=int8, weights=int4. But that'll increase cost ~15-25%.
Ana: worth an A/B. I'll create a canary config: prefetch_limit=1024, kv.trim_threshold=0.7, compactor.rate=0.2, max_new_tokens=256, mixed-dequant=false initially on 10% traffic. Monitor: convo-coherence score, p95, OOM rate, cost/token.
Hannah: add rollback triggers: OOMs > 0.02% OR coherence drop > 2% OR p95 regress > 20% vs baseline.
Sam: I'll draft the mixed-dequant canary config and perf script for next run (if canary proves safe).
Ana: starting canary -> canary-id=pelican-canary-2024-09-10, targets=10% traffic.
Ops-bot: Canary deployed: pelican-canary-2024-09-10 -> see dashboard https://ops.internal/canaries/pelican-canary-2024-09-10
Ana: 18h update: OOMs=0, coherence delta -0.9%, p95 +5%, cost/token -2.7x. Rolling to 50% tomorrow.
Rohit: great. Follow-up: add "int4-hybrid-recipe" to model onboarding docs recommending prefetch_limit<=1024 and default max_new_tokens=256 for convo-facing endpoints.
Ana: will add PR to model-configs with the recipe and link to perf run. Closing loop for now. :rocket:
